title: Best AI customer service companies for 2027
summary: Compare the best AI customer service companies for 2027, organized by company type, vertical fit, and what kind of AI they actually offer.
body_markdown:
## Enterprise AI agent platforms


These companies operate at enterprise scale across multiple industries. They handle complex, multi-step workflows and serve buyers with dedicated engineering resources and six-figure automation budgets.


### Sierra


Sierra deploys AI agents across chat, email, and voice for large consumer and retail brands. The company was co-founded by Bret Taylor (former Salesforce co-CEO) and Clay Bavor (18-year Google veteran) and uses outcome-based pricing tied to business results.


Image source:[Sierra](https://sierra.ai/)


Pros


- Leadership team with proven enterprise credibility
- Outcome-based pricing aligns vendor incentives with results
- Multi-channel resolution across chat, email, and voice


Cons


- [Reported annual minimums around $150,000](https://www.getvocal.ai/blog/why-companies-switch-from-sierra)
- No published pricing, free trial, or self-serve option
- Cross-industry platform, so ecommerce-specific workflows may require more configuration


**Pricing:** Custom enterprise contracts. Outcome-based model with per-resolution rates negotiated per deal.


### Ada


Ada's no-code builder lets non-technical teams design AI conversation flows through SOP-driven playbooks. The platform supports 60 languages and resolves issues across chat, email, voice, SMS, and social. Ada targets enterprise buyers and serves multiple industries.


Image source:[Ada](https://www.ada.cx/)


Pros


- No-code builder accessible to non-technical teams
- Strong multilingual and multi-channel coverage
- SOP playbooks give structure to complex workflows


Cons


- No public pricing. Custom enterprise contracts only
- No native Shopify integration at time of publishing
- [G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/ada-support-inc-ada/reviews/ada-review-11851228) flag integration complexity during workflow setup


**Pricing:** No public pricing page.


## Helpdesk platforms with built-in AI


These companies layer AI onto an existing helpdesk. They work for teams that want one vendor managing both ticketing and automation, though ecommerce teams on Zendesk can also add ecommerce-specific AI through overlay tools like Yuma without switching platforms.


### Zendesk


[Zendesk](https://yuma.ai/blogs/zendesk-ai-vs-yuma-ai-which-actually-automates-e-commerce-support) is one of the largest customer service platforms in the world. Its AI capabilities have expanded significantly[through acquisitions](https://www.zendesk.com/newsroom/press-releases/zendesk-completes-acquisition-of-forethought/) , adding agentic resolution on top of the existing helpdesk architecture. The platform serves every industry and scales to large teams.


Image source:[Zendesk AI](https://www.zendesk.com/service/ai/)


Pros


- Enterprise-grade with a massive integration ecosystem
- Strong reporting and analytics
- Forethought acquisition added agentic AI capabilities
- AI features may work well for companies that are already Zendesk customers and don't have complex automation workflows


Cons


- Pricing stacks multiple layers, which can increase overall cost quickly
- Some ecommerce-specific workflows beyond Shopify may require marketplace apps
- There can be a learning curve for some complex automation features


**Pricing:**[Pricing for plans with AI agents](https://www.zendesk.com/pricing/) starts at $55/agent/month (billed yearly) for Suite plans, with AI features and Copilot billed separately.


### Freshdesk


Freshdesk is a[budget-friendly alternative to Zendesk](https://yuma.ai/blogs/zendesk-ai-alternatives) with Freddy AI for routing, ticket suggestions, and knowledge base deflection. It's simpler to administer and cheaper at equivalent agent counts.


Image source:[Freshdesk](https://www.freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/freddy-ai-copilot/)


Pros


- Lower price point than Zendesk at comparable team sizes
- Free tier available for small teams
- Freddy AI handles routing and suggestions


Cons


- AI capabilities are narrower than Zendesk's post-Forethought stack
- Freddy AI assists agents rather than resolving autonomously
- Ecommerce integrations aren't as deep as purpose-built platforms


**Pricing:**[Free tier available. Paid plans from $29/agent/month.](https://www.freshworks.com/freshdesk/omni/pricing/)


## SaaS and product-led AI


These companies are designed for software businesses where tickets center on product questions, billing issues, and account management rather than order fulfillment.


### Fin (Intercom)


Fin's AI Agent runs on a proprietary model called Apex and resolves conversations across chat, email, voice, SMS, and social in[45+ languages](https://fin.ai/updates/multilingual-fin) . It works standalone with any helpdesk or natively inside Intercom. The distinction between[generative AI and traditional customer support](https://yuma.ai/blogs/ai-and-customer-service-7-reasons-why-generative-ai-outperforms-traditional-customer-support) is clear here, as Fin operates as a true AI agent taking actions through Data Connectors rather than following scripted trees.


Image source:[Fin](https://fin.ai/)


Pros


- Transparent $0.99 per outcome pricing with a low 50-outcome monthly minimum
- 45+ language support
- Fast to deploy with minimal configuration


Cons


- G2 reviewers flag that Fin needs[precise phrasing](https://www.g2.com/products/fin/reviews/fin-review-13188941) for accurate responses
- Ecommerce actions like returns and subscription management require custom API work
- [Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin](https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2026/09/10/salesforce-completes-acquisition-of-fin/) in September 2026, which may introduce some uncertainty about future development


**Pricing:**[Standalone at $0.99 per outcome](https://fin.ai/pricing) , 50-outcome monthly minimum.


### Salesforce Agentforce


Agentforce uses an[Atlas Reasoning Engine](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/what-is-a-reasoning-engine/) with native CRM context to resolve service interactions. It's strongest for teams already on Salesforce who want AI that reads directly from their CRM data.[Pricing has shifted multiple times since launch](https://www.getmonetizely.com/blogs/the-doomed-evolution-of-salesforces-agentforce-pricing) , which is worth factoring into any evaluation.


Image source:[Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/how-it-works/)


Pros


- Native Salesforce CRM integration gives agents full customer context
- Supports customer-facing and employee-facing agent deployments
- Large, established brand with an impressive customer roster


Cons


- Three different pricing models running simultaneously (per-conversation, Flex Credits, per-user) can be complex for brands trying to keep track
- Smaller companies may find the pricing hard to justify without clear ROI visibility


Pricing


- Free tier available for Salesforce Foundations plans, but conversations require credits
- [$500 per 100,000 Flex Credits](https://www.salesforce.com/en-us/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/assets/pdf/agentforce/Flex-Credits-Rate-Card-08.31.2026.pdf) , with actions starting at around 20 credits
- [Option to pay per conversation](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=004811240&type=1) at $2 per conversation


## How to choose the right AI customer service company


Once you know which category fits, these three questions help you compare companies within it and build a shortlist you can defend to leadership.


### What type of tickets drive your volume?


Ecommerce tickets like WISMO, returns, and subscription changes need[ecommerce specialists](https://yuma.ai/blogs/ai-ecommerce) that can take actions inside Shopify and Recharge. Product and billing tickets need SaaS-focused tools. General support across verticals fits a helpdesk with built-in AI.


The type of tickets your team handles every day determines which category of company to evaluate first when[choosing an AI tool for an ecommerce business](https://yuma.ai/blogs/how-to-choose-an-ai-tool-for-ecommerce-customer-service) .


### Does it resolve or just respond?


Some[conversational AI customer service tools](https://yuma.ai/blogs/conversational-ai-customer-service) answer questions and route to humans. Others connect to your systems and close tickets autonomously. A tool that tells a customer the refund policy and a tool that[processes the refund](https://yuma.ai/use-cases/sup002-instantly-process-returns-and-refunds-with-zero-agent-time) are solving two different problems. Before committing, ask whether the AI can take the action that resolves the ticket, or whether an agent still needs to step in.


Conversational AI can handle the conversation, while an[AI agent](https://yuma.ai/blogs/ai-chatbot-customer-service) can handle both the conversation and the resolution. Teams that buy a conversational tool expecting autonomous actions run into the kind of[AI customer service implementation mistakes](https://yuma.ai/blogs/top-6-implementation-mistakes-that-kill-ai-customer-service-and-what-to-do-instead) that set the whole project back.


### What does pricing actually cover?


Per-agent models (Zendesk, Freshdesk) give predictable monthly costs but don't tie spend to what the AI resolves. Per-resolution and per-outcome models (Fin, Gorgias) scale with output but can spike during peak months. Outcome-based models (Yuma, Sierra) only charge for fully resolved tickets, aligning vendor incentives with your results.


The pricing model you choose affects how your costs grow alongside your ticket volume. A per-agent model costs the same whether the AI resolves 500 tickets or 5,000. A per-resolution model rewards high automation but means a busy BFCM week hits your bill directly. Outcome-based pricing ties your spend to actual results, which makes cost easier to justify to leadership when it's time to renew.


## Skip the feature comparison and match the company type to your operation first


Comparing features across[customer service automation](https://yuma.ai/blogs/customer-service-automation) tools built for different buyers is where evaluation time gets wasted. An ecommerce specialist and an enterprise cross-industry platform aren't solving the same problem, and ranking them on the same criteria produces a misleading picture.


Start with the category. If your ticket volume runs through Shopify and your team lives in Gorgias or Zendesk, ecommerce specialists like Yuma will get you to autonomous resolution faster than configuring a cross-industry platform for your workflows. If you're running a SaaS product with billing and account tickets, helpdesk-native or product-led tools are the better fit.


Once you know the category, the shortlist shrinks to two or three companies rather than nine, and the evaluation gets a lot more productive.
